# Bento Land — instructions for Gemini
These apply to every prompt in this project.
## 1. Keep NOTES.md updated as you go
Maintain a file called `NOTES.md` at the project root. Use exactly this structure:
```markdown # Notes
## Finished 1. ... 2. ...
## Next 1. ... 2. ...
## Judgment calls 1. ... 2. ... ```
Rules for maintaining it: - If `NOTES.md` doesn't exist yet, create it with this structure the first time you touch the project. - After any change you make (new screen, new API call, fix, etc.), add a new numbered line to **Finished** describing it in one short sentence. - If something is left incomplete or deferred, add a numbered line to **Next**. - Any time you have to interpret something ambiguous in the design or the API — a field that's missing, a state the design doesn't show, a naming mismatch, a spacing/color guess — add a numbered line to **Judgment calls** explaining what you chose and why. - Append new numbers to the end of each list; don't renumber or delete existing entries unless I ask you to. - Do this without being asked in every prompt — treat it as part of finishing any task, the same way you'd save a file.
## 2. Never silently change a dependency or SDK version
Do not upgrade, downgrade, or otherwise change any version already set in the project — Android Gradle Plugin (AGP), Kotlin, `compileSdk`, `targetSdk`, `minSdk`, Gradle wrapper version, or any library/dependency version — even if you believe a newer or older version would fix a build error.
If you hit a problem that seems to require a version change: 1. Stop before editing any Gradle file. 2. Tell me what's broken, which version you think needs to change, from what to what, and why. 3. Wait for me to confirm before making the edit.
This applies even to transitive/suggested fixes from Android Studio's own "upgrade available" prompts — surface them to me, don't apply them yourself.
